facts.title: Building the Texas Broadband Workforce Grant Program
facts.value: $24.6M; seven grantees; projected 2,800 Texans trained in fiber installation, maintenance and repair.
facts.note: Programs include tuition-free industry-aligned training and work-based learning. Availability and enrollment are provider-specific; use current grantee pages for participant access.

facts.title: Texas broadband mapping layer
facts.value: BDO provides Texas broadband/BEAD map resources and says BEAD project maps will be updated as deployment progresses.
facts.note: Some underlying location data are restricted by FCC licensing. Use official map interfaces and permitted exports rather than redistributing restricted fabric data.

facts.title: Texas State Training Inventory
facts.value: TWC inventory supports searching education and workforce training providers/programs by region, ZIP and field of study
facts.note: Useful for connecting broadband workforce or digital-skills plans to actual training supply.

facts.title: Technical Assistance Program county broadband planning
facts.value: 32 Texas counties were accepted for no-cost broadband planning and consulting assistance; the BDO page identifies plans as complete or finalizing by county.
facts.note: County plans provide localized planning inputs. They should be combined with current FCC/BDO availability and local evidence before project selection.

facts.title: Texas Small Business Resource Portal
facts.value: State portal produces customized resource lists for starting or growing a business, including funding, licensing/permitting, training and local resources
facts.publisher: Office of the Texas Governor — Economic Development & Tourism
facts.note: Users should review the portal privacy/public-disclosure notice before submitting information.

facts.title: Healthcare Connect Fund
facts.value: 65% discount on eligible broadband connectivity expenses for eligible rural health care providers
facts.note: Eligibility and competitive-bidding requirements apply. FY2027 request-for-services activity began July 1, 2026.

facts.title: Texas Middle Mile Program
facts.value: Up to $200M from the Broadband Infrastructure Fund for middle-mile construction/improvement, with resiliency, open-access and affordability objectives.
facts.note: Applications closed Nov. 20, 2025. The current official page says applications are being evaluated and awardees are expected to be notified; verify award status before relying on a proposed project.

facts.title: Texas library broadband role
facts.value: TSLAC treats public-library broadband as infrastructure for workforce, education/training and health access and recommends the Toward Gigabit Libraries Toolkit
facts.publisher: Texas State Library and Archives Commission
facts.note: Libraries can also use E-Rate and TSLAC digital-opportunity resources.

facts.title: FCC National Broadband Map and challenge process
facts.value: The FCC map shows provider-reported fixed/mobile availability and supports availability/location challenges; it does not by itself measure price, adoption, reliability or a household’s experienced performance.
facts.note: Use map vintage and challenge status. Keep provider-reported availability separate from speed tests and community observations.

facts.title: 2026 Texas State Match Fund for E-Rate
facts.value: Up to $5,000,000 in Texas state match funds for eligible school-system E-Rate special-construction projects.
facts.note: Eligibility depends on project type, E-Rate filing status, BDO service-availability data and statutory requirements. Funding windows close; verify current guidance.

facts.title: Texas FY2026 E-Rate State Match and current FY2025 service/invoice dates
facts.value: Texas offered up to $5M in FY2026 state match funding. TEA lists Sept. 30, 2026 as the FY2025 non-recurring service delivery deadline and Oct. 28, 2026 as the FY2025 recurring-service invoice deadline.
facts.note: E-Rate rules and dates are funding-year-specific. Verify USAC/TEA before filing. This suite does not determine eligibility.

facts.title: Texas Digital Opportunity Plan and current funding context
facts.value: Texas Digital Opportunity Plan accepted March 28, 2024; BDO says the State Digital Equity Capacity Grant funding intended to support the roadmap was later terminated, and the office is seeking alternative avenues.
facts.note: The plan remains useful as a barrier/strategy framework. Do not assume a named digital-equity grant remains funded or open without current official confirmation.

facts.title: BOOT I and BOOT II infrastructure awards
facts.value: BOOT I: $10.4M for 1,468 residences, 77 businesses and 15 community anchor institutions. BOOT II: $623.4M for 61,185 residences, 18,250 businesses and 2,191 community anchor institutions.
facts.note: BOOT I projects must be completed by Dec. 31, 2026. BDO publishes monthly awardee status files. BOOT II uses project-specific deadlines; verify each award separately.

facts.title: Texas Broadband Infrastructure Fund
facts.value: Texas voters approved Proposition 8 in 2023; the fund began with a $1.5B investment and is described by BDO as active from 2024 through 2035.
facts.note: The fund supports multiple purposes, including broadband infrastructure, 9-1-1 upgrades, pole replacement and BEAD matching. Program allocations and availability vary.

facts.title: Texas public-sector digital accessibility
facts.value: Texas DIR identifies state/local government, public education, public hospitals/clinics, libraries, transit and other public entities as subject to digital-accessibility requirements
facts.note: The OS targets WCAG 2.2 AA as a design goal; regulated entities should consult current legal/agency requirements.

facts.title: Texas libraries as digital-opportunity hubs
facts.value: TSLAC describes digital opportunity as combining affordable robust broadband, suitable devices, digital skills, technical support and usable online content/services.
facts.publisher: Texas State Library and Archives Commission
facts.note: Libraries can be access/support hubs, but local staffing, privacy, accessibility, bandwidth and space constraints must be assessed rather than assumed.

facts.title: Texas Broadband Pole Replacement Program — dashboard snapshot
facts.value: $51,026,029.31 total available amount including accrued interest; $28,297,960.61 reimbursed; 31 applications awarded as of Aug. 31, 2026.
facts.note: Dashboard values can change as reimbursements and interest change. The program reimburses eligible replacement costs subject to statutory/program rules.

facts.title: 2026 Pediatric Tele-Connectivity Resource Program for Rural Texas
facts.value: HHSC released a 2026 grant opportunity intended to connect rural hospitals/clinics with pediatric specialists or participating higher-education institutions through telemedicine.
facts.publisher: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
facts.note: The listed 2026 application deadline has passed. Preserve as a program/evidence example and verify any successor opportunity before action.

facts.title: Texas emergency-warning continuity emphasis
facts.value: TDEM's April 2026 statewide drill asked local alerting authorities to exercise primary, alternate and contingency warning systems
facts.note: Useful planning precedent for resilient communications; this OS does not replace official alerting systems.

facts.title: DIR TEX-AN and public-sector connectivity procurement
facts.value: DIR describes TEX-AN as competitively procured voice, data and internet connectivity services for eligible public-sector organizations
facts.note: Eligibility and contract terms must be checked with DIR.

facts.title: LCRA middle-mile/flood-monitoring broadband grant
facts.value: $29M state grant announced for LCRA to expand rural middle-mile connectivity and strengthen flood-monitoring infrastructure in Central Texas.
facts.note: An award announcement is not the same as completed construction. Track engineering, construction, activation and public-service outcomes separately.

facts.title: Texas BEAD final proposal — approved program snapshot
facts.value: 22 selected applicants; more than 240,000 broadband-serviceable locations; more than 2,700 community anchor institutions; $1.2B federal grant funding + $177M state match
facts.note: The official BDO page says the Final Proposal was approved Dec. 4, 2025. Treat approved awards, executed grant agreements, construction, activation and subscriber adoption as separate lifecycle states.

facts.title: Texas BEAD technology mix in NTIA overview
facts.value: 242,903 eligible locations: 122,994 FTTP (50.6%); 65,901 LEO satellite (27.1%); 54,008 fixed wireless (22.3%)
facts.note: NTIA overview says data were based on Final Proposal submissions and subject to curing/NIST review at publication.

facts.title: Texas Rural Hospital Broadband Infrastructure Program
facts.value: $23.885M allocated; the 2025 CPF performance report described 124 hospitals in 113 counties, including eight priority projects and 116 network-improvement grants.
facts.publisher: Texas Department of Agriculture / Texas BDO CPF report
facts.note: The application period is closed. Treat infrastructure completion and clinical/telehealth outcomes separately; connectivity investment does not by itself establish health outcomes.

facts.title: Texas public-library LIFI broadband/facility grants
facts.value: $4,107,388 awarded to 37 public libraries for 2025–26 projects; eligible uses include broadband infrastructure and spaces supporting education, work and health monitoring.
facts.publisher: Texas State Library and Archives Commission
facts.note: TSLAC describes LIFI as broadband/facility infrastructure support. A separate broader CPF allocation supports the program; this figure is the 2025–26 award round.

facts.title: Libraries Connecting Texas / E-Rate support snapshot
facts.value: TSLAC commission minutes reported support for 169 library systems, more than $1.35M in discount funding requests and an average discount of 83%.
facts.publisher: Texas State Library and Archives Commission
facts.note: This is a program administration snapshot, not a statewide measure of library bandwidth or need.

facts.title: Texas public-library speed-test context
facts.value: TSLAC reported in its 2025 speed-test dashboard summary that about half of Texas public libraries met or exceeded the relevant FCC benchmark used in that analysis.
facts.publisher: Texas State Library and Archives Commission
facts.note: This is a library-program dashboard interpretation, not a statewide household broadband estimate. Consult the dashboard/source methodology before comparison.

facts.title: Census digital-access measurement tables
facts.value: ACS tables S2801/B28002/B28003 provide household computer and internet-subscription measures; latest source surfaced here is 2024 ACS
facts.note: Use Census geographies and margins of error when comparing counties/tracts; do not equate subscription with service quality.

programs.action: Use the live dashboard for fund/reimbursement status.

programs.action: Route interested learners to current grantee enrollment information and verify local availability.

programs.status: Awarded rounds / verify current NOFO status
programs.action: Verify current grant round; use facilities, bandwidth, accessibility and community-service needs together.

programs.action: Use published county plans as local planning evidence and update with current map/provider data.

programs.status: Plan active as framework; original capacity-grant funding terminated
programs.who: Communities, libraries, nonprofits, planners and support organizations
programs.action: Use the barrier framework; verify separately funded implementation opportunities.

programs.name: Healthcare Connect Fund
programs.who: Eligible rural health care providers / consortia
programs.action: Check RHC Connect for current eligibility, bidding and funding-year deadlines.
